elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 4.1 retains "shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" with no mutual-written-agreement renewal, and the conditional preferred elements (30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder) are not all met, so the automatic-renewal carve-out is unavailable.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: "automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" — renewal term is one (1) year, i.e. no longer than 12 months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause gives the Company sixty (60) days' written notice, not 30 days or fewer. To meet the preferred level the Company's window would have to read thirty (30) days.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in rendered Section 4.1; the proposal adds none and the comment does not promise one.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the cited renewal provision contains no renewal-pricing or uplift mechanic, and no price-escalation language appears in the operative text under review (consideration is a fixed share of Net Sales), so no cap is engaged.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered: "unless terminated by the Company upon sixty (60) days, or by HDI upon ninety (90) days, written notice to the other." The Company (Customer alias) can stop the automatic one-year renewal on a single contiguous 60-day written-notice period, satisfying the ≤60-day ceiling; the deterministic window check confirms this after alias normalization.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition not triggered: the rendered clause and the renewal mechanic contain no price-increase or uplift right, so no cap is required. (The mapping's supporting quote is the renewal sentence rather than any pricing text, which is consistent with there being no uplift mechanic to cap.)

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the Customer's non-renewal window is expressly reduced to sixty (60) days and the price-cap element is inapplicable because no renewal uplift mechanic exists in the operative text.

Preferred level remains incomplete for three named defects the drafter would have to repair in operative language: (i) no mutual-written-agreement renewal (auto-renewal retained), (ii) the Company's window is 60 days rather than thirty (30) days, and (iii) no express Vendor obligation to notify the Company at least sixty (60) days before each renewal. These are correctly noted rather than pressed.

Minimal: the single operation touches only the notice-window phrase needed to reach the fallback, splitting "either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days" into party-specific windows. HDI's ninety-day window is retained (Customer-favourable, harder Vendor exit), and no survival tail, reminder mechanic, uplift cap, or other extra requirement is added.

Preserves intent: the Effective Date trigger, one-year initial term, automatic one-year renewal, "written notice to the other" direction and the "Termination Date" definition all survive verbatim; no dangling cross-reference or undefined term is created and the retained HDI limb does not contradict the new Company limb.

Rationale overstates one point: a ninety (90) day window is not itself walk-away under the stated threshold ("longer than 90 days"), so the original clause is a fallback failure at the boundary, not a walk-away. This is a rationale-wording issue only and does not affect the rendered language or the deviation classification.
Severity remains medium: exit friction on a one-year auto-renewal with no pricing exposure.
